item.title: Iris Sets Auction Record: Monet canvas fetches €50mn in Paris; France hails new mark
item.description: At a Paris auction, Claude Monet's painting titled Iris fetched an astounding 50 million euros, setting a new record for artwork sold in France. The event not only celebrated this remarkable sale but also marked the centenary of Monet's passing, with three more of his exquisite paintings featured at the auction. Additionally, Christie's auction saw impressive sales from a variety of artworks, including several by Monet.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Police Labrador rescues missing 70-year-old hiker in Hawaii; he now wants to adopt her
item.description: After missing for over a day in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, 70-year-old David Arai was successfully located by Trina, a skilled police dog, who led the search team through dense foliage. Found two miles from his rental car and suffering from dehydration, Arai expressed immense gratitude to his rescuers and is now contemplating adopting Trina, who has proven her tracking abilities with two recent rescues.

item.title: New Study Of Westminster Sarcophagus: Roman coffin holds medieval abbot; identity still debated
item.description: Excavations at Westminster Abbey have unveiled a medieval abbot's remains within an ancient Roman coffin, dated to the time between AD 987 and 1052. Notable candidates for the identity of this abbot include Ælfwig and Wulfnoth, who once steered the Westminster Benedictine monastery. The coffin, rich in history, has been preserved and examined since its 19th-century discovery, and today, visitors can appreciate its elaborate inscriptions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Paul Walker founded a Haiti relief group in 2010; it helped 13,093 people in 2025
item.description: A decade after the untimely death of actor Paul Walker, his humanitarian endeavor, Reach Out WorldWide, is creating a significant impact. In 2025 alone, ROWW assisted over 13,000 individuals through various global disaster-relief initiatives. This organization mobilizes skilled volunteers to meet immediate community demands following calamities, operating at no cost to families in need, all while upholding Walker's legacy of providing swift assistance during crises.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ontario farmer rejects C$16 million offer to protect his 164-acre fruit farm
item.description: Charles Stevens and his family have decided to protect Wilmot Orchards by placing a conservation easement on the property. This easement effectively restricts future development for nearly 1,000 years, ensuring continued agricultural use. Their decision counters pressures from developers seeking to convert farmland into housing. The Stevens family aims to preserve the land for future generations of farmers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Finnish watchmaker Kari Voutilainen’s limited-edition steel watch sells for $1.016 million at auction
item.description: At a recent Phillips auction, an exquisite stainless-steel timepiece crafted by renowned watchmaker Kari Voutilainen commanded an impressive $1.016 million, far surpassing its estimated value. The Voutilainen 28Sport Limited Edition features a stunning blue guilloché dial complemented by a striking black onyx center. Originally acquired in 2021, this watch's sale underscores the increasing allure of exceptional and rare watches within the collector community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Portland man turns $48,412 backyard makeover into $85,000 rental business
item.description: Rob Nachbar skillfully turned his once-simple backyard in Portland into a thriving rental space known as Pong Springs. This five-year renovation, which cost $48,412, prioritized weather-resistant structures and enhanced privacy features. Since its launch on Swimply, Nachbar has generated approximately $106,000 in revenue. The yard not only hosts various events but also provides the family with a serene private retreat—combining leisure and financial success.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Jason Momoa buys Queenstown estate for NZ$15 million, NZ$3.5 million above valuation
item.description: Jason Momoa has recently acquired a significant property in Queenstown, New Zealand for NZ$15 million. The estate, formerly owned by Sir Sam Neill, demonstrates the increasing interest in the local real estate market. Property values in the region have risen significantly, attracting overseas buyers. Momoa has deep connections to New Zealand, having visited frequently for leisure and work. He has also invested in the local film industry and nightlife scene.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas farmer grows from 27 to 10,000 sheep by grazing solar farms across 40,000 acres
item.description: JR Howard experienced hardships early on with only a small number of sheep, making it tough to earn a living. However, after landing a grazing contract with solar farms, he expanded his flock and income significantly. This eco-friendly grazing method is being embraced by renewable energy companies as a cost-effective way to manage vegetation, while farmers benefit from expansive grazing land without hefty property expenses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California family spends $4,000 and 200 hours turning its yard into a free Jurassic Park attraction
item.description: In Granada Hills, a family has dedicated $4,000 to create an elaborate Jurassic Park-themed display for Halloween. After investing over 200 hours, they've constructed life-sized dinosaur replicas and an automated escape show, complete with grand entrance gates. Open to the public at no cost, this attraction fosters community spirit as neighbors flock to capture the experience and enjoy this festive installation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Media Losses Cloud Empire: MrBeast’s $5bn business leans on his fame; long-term durability in doubt
item.description: MrBeast has transformed his YouTube fame into a business empire valued at $5 billion, spanning chocolate, television and financial technology. His Feastables brand generated $250 million in sales and over $20 million in profit in 2024. However, his media business lost nearly $80 million despite strong revenue. With major investor backing and a fintech acquisition reaching seven million users, MrBeast faces the challenge of turning online popularity into sustainable, profitable businesses.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'He put it back': Trump says Ukraine's Starlink restored, stays silent on Musk
item.description: Ukraine depends heavily on Starlink for communications between military units, coordinating operations and receiving early warnings during Russian missile attacks. The satellite-based network also supports the use of drones, which Ukraine deploys both to strike Russian targets and to defend against incoming attacks. Disruptions to connectivity can therefore affect the military's ability to operate drones and respond to Russian assaults.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Goose Creek Estate Listed: Quirky 1958 ranch hits market at $1.227 million; licensed short-term rental
item.description: Nestled at 108 Hampton Avenue, this unique property in Goose Creek is now on the market. It boasts three distinct kitchens, creatively themed bedrooms, and a generous indoor pool. Spanning 5,390 square feet, this estate is perfect for multigenerational families or as a lucrative short-term rental option. The outdoor spaces are ideal for entertaining.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Necklace nearly sold for £15 at car boot sale fetches £99,000 at auction
item.description: Imagine a dusty car boot sale where a unique necklace fashioned from human hair and whale bone was nearly sold for just £15. Fortunately, it caught the eye of an expert at Ewbank's auction house, revealing its immense worth, which fetched an incredible £99,000 at auction. This story underscores the vital role of appraisals in recognizing hidden treasures that often go unnoticed in clearance sales.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
